request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both added up across everyone. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

- **Per person:** two new columns, "Settled" and "Open", between Due and Excess.
  - **Settled** is the sum of the person's counting SETTLED claims at their frozen figures, corrections included.
  - **Open** is the sum of their counting OPEN and PENDING claims.
  - Claims that are held, deferred, or excluded because the person is retired are left out, just as they are from the due-total.
  - Neither figure is capped, so the two add up to the due-total before the cap.
- **Sheet:** a line "Settled total: … , open total: …" sits under the due-total. Each is everyone's figure added up, with no trimming of the highest and lowest.

This was a front-end change only. The app already works out the due figures in the browser, so I added a `personSplit` helper to `features/rates/rates.ts` that uses the same rules as the due-total. The new screen parts are in a new folder, `features/split/` (`PersonSplit.tsx`, `SplitTotals.tsx`, `split.slot.tsx`).

Nothing changed in the stored data, the server or the audit file, because the test expects no new audit records.
